M19 remains top, followed by M18, M9, M13. These all involve catalyst deactivation. The low-substrate experiment didn't cleanly separate them—M18/M19 still fit well perhaps because turnover is fast enough that catS still forms. M12 (product inhibition) also fits reasonably.

<hypothesis>
To distinguish among M19 (cat+catS→dead), M18 (2catS→dead), M9 (cat→dead), M13 (2cat→dead), and M12 (P inhibition):

- Add significant initial product with high [cat]: This tests M12 vs. deactivation. M12 predicts slower initial rate; deactivation mechanisms should show similar initial rate as P=0 case.
- M9 has 1st order cat decay; predicts exponential decay of catalyst activity independent of [S] or [P].
- M13 needs 2 free cat, so at high [S] (most catalyst as catS), M13 decay stops → less stalling.
- M18 needs 2 catS, so at low [S], less stalling.
- M19 needs both cat and catS, so depends on both.

Best discriminator: high [S] with high [cat] — most catalyst is catS, so:
- M13 (needs 2 cat): little deactivation → high final conversion
- M18 (needs 2 catS): strong deactivation → stalling
- M19 (cat+catS): moderate deactivation
- M9 (cat alone): steady deactivation regardless
- M12 (P inhibition): strong slowdown as P builds

Predictions for [S]=3.0, [cat]=0.05, [P]=0:
- M13: high conversion, no stalling
- M18: strong stalling at intermediate conversion
- M19: moderate stalling
- M9: deactivation continues; stalling
- M12: slowdown at high conversion (high P)
</hypothesis>
